Subject: Aurora - private endpoint networking evidence request

Hi Laura,

Thanks for the demo last week — Aurora is moving toward embedding Redwood in our on‑prem private deployment and the auditors have asked us to collect explicit networking evidence for the private endpoint. To keep things scoped, could you provide a concise technical pack we can present to our security and procurement folks that includes: 

- Static/per‑region egress IPs or CIDRs we should allow on our firewall (and whether they are guaranteed or best‑effort).
- FQDNs and ports to allow for the control plane, token exchange, telemetry, and model inference egress.
- Expected TLS behavior (SNI, certificate chains), and whether mutual TLS is required/supported for control plane vs. runtime.
- How ephemeral IP rotation is handled and communication cadence for rotation windows.
- Any DNS/TCP behavior that might require special handling (e.g., outbound DNS to 3rd party resolvers, alternate ports, ALPN expectations).
- Sample statement or attestation we can hand to the auditor that summarizes Redwood’s egress/allowlist controls.

We have a target date to sign off on networking controls by EOD 2027‑01‑10 to stay on the onboarding timeline. If you can send us the pack and any diagrams today/tomorrow that would be ideal. If helpful, we can do a short call (30m) with NetOps and Security.

Appreciate it —
Maya
Maya Rivera
Senior Information Security Manager
Aurora Health

Hi all —

Attaching the technical snapshot and diagram. Key points (summary):

1) IPs/CIDRs (static per‑region binding)
- us‑west‑1: 34.201.120.32/28, 34.201.121.16/28 (these are reserved egress addresses for control plane and model pull).
- us‑east‑1: 35.190.250.0/28, 35.190.250.16/28.
- eu‑west‑1: 18.194.220.0/28 (if you deploy into a Redwood private cloud in EU we’ll provide EU‑only ranges).

Notes: These are the current published static egress ranges we allocate for private deployments with reserved capacity. For some hosted burst and telemetry flows we may use short‑lived IPs; those are marked in the CSV with an "ephemeral" flag. We guarantee the static entries above for Reserved Capacity contracts; ephemeral ranges are best‑effort and may rotate on a monthly cadence with 72h pre‑notice.

2) Ports/FQDNs to allow
- Outbound TCP 443 to: controlplane.redwood-inference.com, auth.redwood-inference.com, telemetry.redwood-inference.com, models-us.redwood-inference.com (SNI will be present; do not rely on IP only).
- DNS: outbound UDP/TCP 53 to your resolvers is fine. If you perform egress DNS interception, ensure FQDNs above resolve to the published IPs per region.
- Optional telemetry agent: outbound 443 to telemetry.redwood-inference.com (mutual TLS not required for runtime telemetry; control plane supports mTLS for higher assurance).

3) NAT and routing behavior
- In private (VPC/on‑prem) installs the runtime performs SNAT at the customer egress. For Redwood‑managed private control plane connections we terminate TLS from the runtime to Redwood endpoints; no inbound open ports are required.
- If you need single‑IP pinning, we can provision a dedicated egress IP pool under the Reserved Capacity contract and provide an SLA for those addresses.

4) Rotation and notices
- Ephemeral IP pools rotate monthly; we publish an excel/CSV with a 72h change window. Static pools are only changed with contract and 30‑day notice.

5) Attachments included
- egress-ip-list-january-2027.csv (columns: region, ip_cidr, type[static|ephemeral], notes)
- private-endpoint-egress-diagram.png

If you need a CIDR expressed as a single IP for a vendor allowlist, the CSV has a mapping and a recommended /32 per service. Happy to walk through the diagram on a call.

— Jordan
Jordan Blake
Senior Network Engineer, Redwood Inference

Hi Maya —

Adding the security posture notes and the attestation template (see attachment). High‑level recommendations for your firewall and auditor: 

- Allow outbound TCP 443 to the FQDNs Jordan listed. We recommend FQDN+SNI allow rules rather than only IPs where possible to handle rotation.
- Require TLS 1.2+ and disable SSLv3/TLSv1.0. Our control plane and runtime use modern cipher suites; we publish the accepted ciphers in the attached checklist.
- SNI inspection: permitted. Note that SNI is required for routing in some multi‑tenant setups; do not strip SNI.
- Mutual TLS: supported for control plane (can be enabled per customer). For routine inference traffic, mTLS is optional; we sign tokens short lived (60s – 5m) so token exchange is primary auth.
- DNS considerations: if you perform DNS whitelisting, ensure you are querying resolvers that will resolve Redwood FQDNs to the published IPs; we recommend a cache TTL of >=60s to avoid excessive queries during rotations.
- Telemetry/Logging: we can provide an evidence bundle that includes connection attempt logs (timestamped) for a requested 30‑day window — we’ll need a signed DPA addendum to ship logs for production tenants.

Attached: egress-checklist-security.md (contains ciphers, sample firewall ACL rules, and an attestation template). I also drafted the attestation statement you can present to your auditor — feel free to redline.

Neha Kapoor
Principal Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
